audits.title: Improving the quality of nursing documentation at a residential care home: a clinical audit.
audits.standard: N-Catch II audit instrument: complete documentation (score 3) for admission assessment, nursing diagnoses, aims, interventions and evaluation

cycle1.result: No records met standards; mean scores from 0.4 (aims for nursing care) to 1.1 (nursing diagnoses).

audits.intervention: Tailored multifaceted implementation strategy addressing local barriers.

cycle2.result: Improvement reported but standards not yet met (figures truncated in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Further audit cycles needed before standards are met.
audits.citation: Moldskred PS, Snibsøer AK, Espehaug B. Improving the quality of nursing documentation at a residential care home: a clinical audit. BMC Nurs. 2021;20(1):103. doi:10.1186/s12912-021-00629-9. PMID: 34154606.

audits.title: A comparison of quality of care using Phaneuf's Nursing Audit.
audits.setting: Professional Nursing Unit and general hospital wards, diabetes patients

cycle1.result: Professional Nursing Unit mean scores were 26.4% higher than those of general hospital wards.

audits.other_findings: Major variations in scores in specific areas of care.
audits.citation: Pearson A, Baker H. A comparison of quality of care using Phaneuf's Nursing Audit. Aust Clin Rev. 1992;12(1):41-48. PMID: 1586295.

audits.title: Nursing documentation audit--the effect of a VIPS implementation programme in Denmark.
audits.standard: VIPS model for nursing documentation (Cat-ch-Ing instrument)
audits.setting: Cardiology, neurology, oncology and urology departments, Rigshospitalet, Copenhagen
audits.intervention: Structured VIPS implementation programme with training of all nursing staff.

cycle2.result: Documentation significantly improved; keywords used correctly after the second year.

audits.other_findings: 600 journals audited over three years; primary nursing application increased.
audits.citation: Darmer MR, Ankersen L, Nielsen BG, Landberger G, Lippert E, Egerod I. Nursing documentation audit--the effect of a VIPS implementation programme in Denmark. J Clin Nurs. 2006;15(5):525-534. doi:10.1111/j.1365-2702.2006.01475.x. PMID: 16629961.

audits.title: Quality improvement in documentation of postoperative care nursing using computer-based medical records.
audits.standard: Clinical guidelines for postanaesthesia nursing documentation
audits.setting: Department of Anaesthesia and Intensive Care, Odense University Hospital

cycle1.result: Quantitative template: satisfactory documentation in 67% (18% to 92%) of scores; qualitative template used by 63% of nurses with keywords used in 0% to 63%.

audits.intervention: New electronic template with 10 physiological parameters and drop-down keyword lists

cycle2.result: Quality of documentation improved (figures not given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Non-compliance with clinical guidelines and multiple duplicate entries were found.
audits.citation: Olsen SW. Quality improvement in documentation of postoperative care nursing using computer-based medical records. J Perianesth Nurs. 2013;28(2):77-86. doi:10.1016/j.jopan.2012.08.006. PMID: 23522267.

audits.title: Findings From a Nursing Care Audit Based on the Nursing Process: A Descriptive Study.
audits.setting: Clinical settings of Tehran University of Medical Sciences

audits.title: An Audit of Nursing Documentation at Three Public Hospitals in Jamaica.
audits.standard: Audit instrument covering history, assessment, nursing standards, discharge planning and teaching
audits.setting: Medical wards of three public type B hospitals

cycle1.result: Chief complaint documented in 81.6%; physical assessment within 24 hr in 90%; patient teaching in under 5%; discharge planning within 72 hr in 13.5%.

audits.other_findings: Less than a third recorded adequate assessment data such as occupation or living conditions.
audits.citation: Lindo J, Stennett R, Stephenson-Wilson K, Barrett KA, Bunnaman D, Anderson-Johnson P, et al.. An Audit of Nursing Documentation at Three Public Hospitals in Jamaica. J Nurs Scholarsh. 2016;48(5):499-507. doi:10.1111/jnu.12234. PMID: 27459736.

audits.title: Improving the quality of nursing documentation in a palliative care setting: a quality improvement initiative.
audits.standard: Holistic nursing documentation, including WHO palliative care definition of assessment and management of symptoms
audits.setting: Specialist palliative care centre (Milford Care Centre, Limerick)

cycle1.result: Existing documentation focused mainly on physical symptoms, with other aspects less frequently documented.

audits.intervention: New palliative nursing care document and audit tool developed through cycles of review, action and reflection, then piloted.

cycle2.result: Higher compliance with nursing assessments and more concise, comprehensive documentation of holistic care and patients' perspectives.

audits.other_findings: Continuous education and organisational support were needed to sustain results and avoid a tick-box exercise.
audits.citation: Stewart K, Doody O, Bailey M, Moran S. Improving the quality of nursing documentation in a palliative care setting: a quality improvement initiative. Int J Palliat Nurs. 2017;23(12):577-585. doi:10.12968/ijpn.2017.23.12.577. PMID: 29272195.

audits.title: Auditing completion of nursing records as an outcome indicator for identifying patients at risk of developing pressure ulcers, falling, and social vulnerability: An observational study.
audits.standard: Completion of Braden, Downton and Gijón risk scales
audits.setting: COVID-19 hospital units, Hospital Clínico Universitario de Valladolid

cycle1.result: Pre-pandemic vs first vs second wave completion: Braden 40.97%, 28.02%, 30.99%; Downton 43.74%, 22.34%, 33.91%; Gijón 40.12%, 26.23%, 33.64%.

audits.other_findings: Completion fell significantly during the pandemic waves.

Auditing completion of nursing records as an outcome indicator for identifying patients at risk of developing pressure ulcers, falling, and social vulnerability: An observational study.
